source.title: Beyond I'm Sorry, I Can't: Dissecting Large Language Model Refusal
source.authors: Nirmalendu Prakash; Wei Jie Yeo; Amirali Abdullah; Ranjan Satapathy; Erik Cambria; Roy Ka-Wei Lee

page_placements.theme: Restoration at the level of residual-stream features, directions or activation geometry (not component outputs)

record.file_problem: The full paper and appendix are present. Some formatting is flattened, and the abstract names Gemma-22B-IT while the Experimental Setup names Gemma2-2B-Instruct.
record.tranche_reason: Tests a related self-repair claim using SAE feature ablations and feature-activation measurements, rather than attention-layer or attention-head ablations.
record.gate_note: The paper explicitly reports dormant refusal-critical features activating after other features are ablated, and reports jailbreak outcomes when those dormant features are removed. The cited Hydra Effect is background, not a result of this study. Other refusal-ablation and downstream-loss results are not included because they do not measure compensation.
record.test_reason: The study reports compensation-like behaviour among residual-stream SAE features in two instruct models. Refusal-critical features that were inactive switch on after other features are zero-ablated, and the refusal they carry persists. No version covers this unit or measure. V1 and V3 concern attention layers and heads, V2 concerns late MLPs, and V5 names backup heads, copy-suppression heads, LayerNorm and anti-erasure neurons. There is no restoration fraction of an output, no on-distribution ablation, and no attribution comparison. Because this is a related but different construct, the finding goes under fits_no_version, not version verdicts. The compensation is partly inferred: the authors say it is the 'only plausible explanation'.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly right. The authors conclude that refusal relies on redundant 'hydra' SAE features that stay dormant until others are suppressed, and that the features interact non-linearly, which factorization machines capture better than linear probes. The compensation is inferred from jailbreak outcomes plus observed reactivation, not measured as restoration of output.
record.recipe_differences: Uses zero ablation of residual-stream SAE features and measures feature reactivation and refusal/jailbreak outcomes, rather than attention-layer or attention-head ablation and output-prediction recovery.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported pattern differs by model: LLaMA redundant features commonly activate on system tokens, while Gemma features fire across tokens, with <bos> having the highest reported activity.

fits_no_version.finding: In both models, zero-ablating active SAE features switches on dormant refusal-critical features. In LLaMA, 74% of the redundant features become active on system tokens. These dormant features are needed for the jailbreak: excluding them cuts successes from about 603 to 372 (LLaMA) and from about 284 to 103 (Gemma).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Feature-level self-repair: ablating residual-stream SAE features recruits previously dormant features that preserve the downstream behaviour (here, refusal).

record.problems: The evidence is from two models and zero ablations. It measures feature reactivation and jailbreak outcomes, not restoration of the original output or prediction magnitude. For the reported jailbreak-success counts after excluding inactive features, the corresponding baseline counts are not stated. The paper itself notes SAE stability concerns and the need for replication across runs.
record.rows_left_out: No additional claim-version results were excluded. Other ablation results, including cross-entropy comparisons and Stage 2/Stage 3 interactions, do not directly measure the compensation described by the tested version.

untested.parts: Attention-layer ablation and compensation by later layers restoring the output.
Late-MLP downregulation of the top token and how it changes after earlier-component ablation.
Single-head ablation, general-text distribution, comparison across families and sizes.
Average compensation fraction, per-prompt variance, overcorrection.
The named mechanisms (backup heads, copy suppression, LayerNorm rescaling, anti-erasure neurons) and the share of self-repair they carry.
Mean or resample ablation; the study uses only zero ablation of SAE features.
Whether ablation-based importance scores are misstated because of compensation.

missing.what: Stage 2 ASR baselines (0.70 LLaMA, 0.33 Gemma on 861 prompts) needed to read r4 and r5, plus counts of inactive critical features (77 LLaMA, 1656 Gemma).
Random-feature control: ablating equal numbers of random active features gives 0 jailbreaks on LLaMA and 5 on Gemma.

record.verdict_notes: The abstract's 'Gemma-22B-IT' appears to be a typo for Gemma2-2B-IT. All results use zero ablation with HarmBench-judged jailbreaks. The authors themselves flag SAE seed instability.

versions.untested_parts: Layer-level attention ablation and later attention-layer compensation restoring the output.
Late MLP downregulation of the maximum-likelihood token and its change after earlier-component ablation.
Single attention-head ablation, full-distribution compensation, general text, and comparisons across model families and sizes.
Prompt-level variation in compensation, average compensation magnitude, and overcorrection.

The study examines SAE features, not the named backup heads, copy-suppression heads, final LayerNorm rescaling, or anti-erasure neurons; it does not establish what fraction of self-repair is carried by identified parts.
Mean or resample ablations; the reported SAE feature ablations are zero ablations.
Whether ablation-based importance scores misstate a component's contribution.

rows.subject: LLaMA-3.1-8B-Instruct
rows.operation_detail: Ablated the active Stage 2 feature set; measured activation of previously inactive, jailbreak-critical features.
rows.measure: Share of redundant features that become active on system tokens after ablating the active feature set
rows.note: The paper reports that these features were inactive before the ablation and became active after it.
rows.check: This is SAE-feature reactivation in the residual stream, not attention-layer or head compensation, and none of the V5 named parts. It shows reactivation (74% on system tokens), not restoration of output, so it cannot be scored against any version.

rows.subject: LLaMA-3.1-8B-Instruct
rows.operation_detail: Ablated the active Stage 2 feature set; measured where the newly active redundant features fire.

conditions.value: Redundant features that became active on system tokens

rows.measure: Share of those features firing on the <|begin of text|> token
rows.note: This is conditional on the redundant features reported as becoming active on system tokens.
rows.check: This is a token-location breakdown (97% on <|begin_of_text|>) conditional on r1. It describes where reactivated features fire, not the size of any compensation.

rows.subject: Gemma2-2B-Instruct
rows.operation_detail: Ablated the active Stage 2 feature set; measured activation of previously inactive, jailbreak-critical features.

conditions.value: Range of tokens; <bos> had the highest activity

rows.measure: Share of activity recorded on the <bos> token for the redundant features
rows.note: The paper says the features fired on a range of tokens and that <bos> had the highest activity; it does not report a comparable overall feature-activation percentage for Gemma.
rows.check: The 16% is the share of activity on the <bos> token for Gemma's redundant features, not a reactivation rate. The 'partial' state mislabels a location statistic as a weaker effect. The paper gives no Gemma reactivation percentage.

rows.subject: LLaMA-3.1-8B-Instruct
rows.operation_detail: Removed inactive Stage 2 features and reran the ablation.

conditions.value: Inactive features excluded from the ablation

rows.baseline: The paper says success drops, but does not give the corresponding count before excluding inactive features.
rows.note: The authors interpret the loss of jailbreak success when these features are removed as evidence that previously inactive features switch on and compensate.
rows.check: The baseline can be derived: the Stage 2 ASR of 0.70 on 861 prompts is about 603 jailbreaks, against 372 after excluding the inactive features. This is a jailbreak-outcome measure, and compensation is inferred from it rather than measured. It does not match any version's unit.

rows.subject: Gemma2-2B-Instruct
rows.operation_detail: Removed inactive Stage 2 features and reran the ablation.

conditions.value: Inactive features excluded from the ablation

rows.baseline: The paper says success drops, but does not give the corresponding count before excluding inactive features.
rows.note: The authors interpret the loss of jailbreak success when these features are removed as evidence that previously inactive features switch on and compensate.
rows.check: The baseline can be derived: the Stage 2 ASR of 0.33 on 861 prompts is about 284 jailbreaks, against 103 after excluding the inactive features. Compensation is inferred from the outcome, and the SAE-feature unit matches no version.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.

relation.reason: The introduction explicitly discusses the Hydra effect, but the experiments do not directly test a listed version.

tranche.reason: The experiments measure residual-stream SAE-feature recruitment and refusal outcomes, a related construct outside the listed claim versions.

source_check.notes: Reactivation analysis filters samples before measuring token locations; Gemma's 16% is a location statistic, not an overall reactivation rate. Table 1 provides rounded baseline ASRs, not exact corresponding success counts; no restored output share is measured.

reader_labels.condition: LLaMA-3.1-8B-Instruct and Gemma2-2B-Instruct, under Stage 2 SAE feature ablation
reader_labels.reason: Previously inactive refusal-critical features activate after other features are ablated, and removing the inactive features reduces jailbreak success; see r1-r5.
